Cummins Hints at Selection Changes Following Australia's Series Defeat to South Africa

01 Nov 2026, 05:15 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Editorial Desk · Source: www.icc-cricket.com

Original GlobeWire Daily editorial illustration — not an event photograph.

Key takeaways Series Defeat at Newlands Australia captain Pat Cummins has indicated that squad changes could be on the horizon following a 2-1 series defeat to South Africa in the ICC World Test Championship 2025–27 cycle. The deciding Test concluded with Australia being bowled out

Series Defeat at Newlands

Australia captain Pat Cummins has indicated that squad changes could be on the horizon following a 2-1 series defeat to South Africa in the ICC World Test Championship 2025–27 cycle. The deciding Test concluded with Australia being bowled out for 111 on day five while chasing a fourth-innings target of 288, resulting in a 176-run loss at Newlands.

The completed result dropped Australia to three losses in their past five Test matches. According to published reports, top-order batting collapses have emerged as a recurring concern, with several top-order batters averaging under 22 across the series.

Captain's Assessment of the Final Day

Reflecting on the final-day collapse, Cummins addressed tactical choices during the run chase:

  • Tactical Approach: Cummins noted that the team may have overplayed spinner Simon Harmer and failed to back their defense for longer periods.
  • Decision-Making: The captain criticized the top order's decision-making under pressure on a day-five surface.
  • Series Moments: Cummins stated that the series ultimately came down to critical passages of play where South Africa capitalized more effectively.

Implications for the World Test Championship

As part of the broader standings:

  • South Africa claimed the 2-1 series victory.
  • South Africa surpassed Australia to take the top spot in the ICC Men's Test Team Rankings.
  • New Zealand advanced to the top of the World Test Championship Standings.
  • Australia previously won the second Test of the series by an innings and 31 runs.

Outlook and Verification

With upcoming fixtures against New Zealand scheduled for December, Cummins acknowledged that internal discussions regarding team selection and potential shifts in style or personnel are expected.
